# Dependency Time Machine (DTM)

Dependency Time Machine evaluates proposed dependency upgrades before they
merge. It compares base vs candidate dependency graphs, inspects release notes
and security advisories, and produces an evidence-backed risk report plus a CI
check. It is not a package manager and not a Dependabot/Renovate replacement:
those tools propose updates; DTM tests the impact.

## Execution model (read this before interpreting results)

- Container-isolated runner execution (`DTM_RUNNER_MODE=container`) is the
  documented path for actually running builds/tests.
- Safe-degraded mode (no container runtime available) performs
  manifest/graph-level analysis only: dependency graph diff, release-note
  signals, advisory matching. No build or test command is executed, and no
  report claims builds/tests ran. Treat `executed: false` and
  `runnerMode: "degraded"` as "analysis only".
- The API pipeline endpoint always stores runs with `runnerMode: "degraded"`,
  `executed: false`; runs that did execute are ingested via
  `POST /v1/cli-runs` from the CLI/runner.

## Endpoints (Go control plane, JSON)

Base URL in local dev: http://127.0.0.1:8080 (env DTM_HTTP_ADDR).

- POST /v1/upgrade-runs — run a base-vs-candidate upgrade evaluation
  (pipeline: graph diff, release notes, advisories; stores the run;
  201 created, 200 on idempotent replay, 409 on key/content conflict,
  422 on rejected content). Body capped at 2 MiB.
- GET /v1/upgrade-runs/{id} — fetch a stored run summary; 404 when absent.
- GET /v1/upgrade-runs/{id}/graph-diff — the run's dependency-graph diff;
  404 when the run or its diff is absent.
- GET /v1/upgrade-runs/{id}/report — the run's report; JSON by default,
  Markdown when the Accept header contains "markdown"; 404 when absent.
- POST /v1/repositories/connect — register an owner/repo the control plane
  manages (provider defaults to github); returns the project_id.
- POST /v1/snapshots — record one commit's manifest+lockfile contents;
  detects supported ecosystems; 422 when no supported pair is found.
- POST /v1/policies — set a project's block/warn result-class thresholds
  (severities: confirmed_failure, strong_warning, review_suggested,
  no_issue_observed).
- POST /v1/webhooks/github — GitHub event intake; HMAC-SHA256 verified
  (X-Hub-Signature-256) plus X-Hub-Delivery nonce replay guard
  (15-minute in-process window); 202 when accepted, 401 when no secret is
  configured or the signature is invalid, 403 on replayed nonce.
- POST /v1/cli-runs — intake a completed run from the dtm CLI/runner;
  persists it and posts a GitHub check-run when a token is configured
  (honest `posting` field: skipped_no_token | posted | failed: ...).
- GET /healthz — liveness; unauthenticated, unthrottled; 200 {"status":"ok"}.
- GET /readyz — readiness; unauthenticated, unthrottled; 200 {"status":"ready"}
  or 503 {"status":"not_ready"} until the data store is reachable.

## Error envelope

Every non-2xx response is exactly:

    {"error": {"code": "<err_code>", "message": "<human detail>"}}

Error codes: err_unauthorized (401), err_forbidden (403, webhook replay),
err_rate_limited (429, with Retry-After: 1), err_invalid_request (400),
err_payload_too_large (413, over the 2 MiB body cap), err_not_found (404),
err_conflict (409, idempotency-key content mismatch), err_internal (500).

## Authentication

- Operator bearer: when DTM_API_TOKEN is set (>= 16 chars), every /v1/*
  route requires a matching `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header
  (constant-time compare); missing/wrong token is 401. Unset means
  dev-open mode: requests are accepted and a WARN is logged instead.
- Webhook HMAC: /v1/webhooks/github only; per-recipient secret
  (DTM_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET), closed default — no secret, no webhook.

## Rate limits (per client IP, per route class)

- analysis: POST /v1/upgrade-runs — default 20 rps / burst 40.
- webhooks: POST /v1/webhooks/github — default 10 / 20.
- reads: GET /v1/upgrade-runs/{id}[...], report and graph-diff fetches —
  default 50 / 100.
- repos: POST /v1/repositories/connect, /v1/snapshots, /v1/policies,
  /v1/cli-runs — default 5 / 10.

Env knobs: DTM_RATE_LIMIT_<ANALYSIS|WEBHOOKS|READS|REPOS>_RPS/_BURST. A class
left at 0 falls back to the legacy global DTM_RATE_LIMIT_RPS/_BURST (10/20).
GET /healthz and /readyz are never throttled (the container HEALTHCHECK
probes /healthz; it must not 429). Note: limiter counters are per-process;
N replicas get N times the configured budget (see docs/SCALING.md).

## Configuration (selected env vars)

DTM_API_TOKEN (operator auth; off when unset), DTM_CORS_ORIGIN (echoed into
Access-Control-Allow-Origin when set; empty = no CORS header, never `*`),
DTM_DATA_DRIVER (sqlite default | postgres | memory), DTM_HTTP_ADDR
(127.0.0.1:8080), DTM_RUNNER_MODE (auto|container|degraded),
DTM_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, DTM_ARTIFACT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 14).

## Execution guarantees and known limits

- Container-isolated execution is the documented path for builds/tests;
  safe-degraded mode is analysis-only (never claims execution). Details:
  docs/EXECUTION-ISOLATION-LIMITS.md.
- Webhook replay nonces and rate-limit counters are per-process
  (best-effort; a shared store is needed across replicas): docs/SCALING.md.
- GitHub App installation-token exchange is a documented limitation in this
  build; check-run posting works only with a direct operator token:
  docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md.

## Further reading

- docs/API.md — endpoint reference, error-code table, rate-limit class table.
- docs/SCALING.md — statelessness, replica caveats, data store, run persistence.
- docs/EXECUTION-ISOLATION-LIMITS.md — what "degraded mode" and container mode
  each guarantee (and do not guarantee).
- docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md — explicit gaps and honest limitations.
- docs/openapi.yaml — machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0 spec of every route.
